A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Learning-to-Theorize/NEO work. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison. The reduction from 43 to 42 pages reflects layout changes, not missing material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on GridWorld, Arithmetic Factorization Reasoning, and CIFAR-10 image editing, including generalization results, ablations, and test-time scaling.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendices C–F, including the benchmark comparisons in Tables 1, 2, and 11.

M1.justification: The primitive codebook, theory programmer, shared executor, MDL length selection, grounding loss, and inference procedures are unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix B. The new 'World Theory Model' description does not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three OTIB domains: GridWorld, Arithmetic Factorization Reasoning, and CIFAR-10 image editing, with the same in-distribution, compositional OOD, and length OOD scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 11 retain Disc-Mono, Cont-Mono, and Cont-Mono-Opt in the same comparisons. The identity-baseline reference in Appendix C.7.1 is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported alpha splits, support/query evaluation, program-length limits, metrics, sample sizes, training settings, and sampling budgets are unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices C, D, and F.

E4.justification: The grounding-loss, codebook-size, and MDL ablations, primitive-alignment analyses, test-time scaling studies, and rollout examples are retained. Resizing Figure 8 and relocating Figure 9 do not add or remove analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report means over three runs in Tables 1, 2, and 11, three-seed information in Appendix F, and the same plotted variability. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains NEO's GridWorld transfer scores of 0.933 for compositional OOD and 0.845 for length OOD at alpha = 0.33.

T1.justification: The program definitions, assumptions, probabilistic factorization, variational objective, MDL criterion, grounding formulation, and appendix metric definitions are unchanged. Equation reflow introduces no mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about learning executable theories and compositional generalization. Calling NEO a 'World Theory Model' names its existing role without changing the claims' meaning or scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of primitive discovery, grounding, and test-time search remain unchanged, as do Section 6's limitations. Figure 1's new 'Prediction-centric Approach' label restates the contrast already developed in v1.

D1.justification: Pseudocode, data-construction instructions, hardware and runtime information, and hyperparameters in Appendices B–F are unchanged. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive comparisons with prior research remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix G. Removing the URL from Ellis et al. (2016) is bibliographic editing; the new model label preserves the existing positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction adds one sentence describing NEO as a 'World Theory Model.' Figure 1 replaces 'Memorization' with 'Prediction-centric Approach,' and one reference is shortened. The narrative and section organization otherwise remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is revised with arrows between observation pairs and a renamed panel. Appendix spacing is tightened and Figure 8 reduced in size so Figure 9 fits beneath it instead of occupying a separate page. Other changes are local text and reference reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 makes limited terminology and diagram edits and compacts the appendix, with Figure 8 becoming smaller. These changes leave the argument and its presentation materially equivalent; the scientific evidence, reproducibility information, and stated limitations are unchanged. No meaningful overall quality gain or loss is established.
